ai.title: Fix React 19 key prop warning in typescript-viewer
ai.summary: Refactored token rendering in `typescript-viewer.tsx` to prevent React 19 key prop warnings. Explicitly extracts and discards `key` from `getLineProps` and `getTokenProps` return objects before spreading remaining props. This ensures React controls the key generation without conflicting with the library's provided keys. Scope limited to `web/src/components/agent/typescript-viewer.tsx`.

eli5.text: The code that shows highlighted code examples in your browser now displays each piece of text without flashing a confusing warning message to developers who maintain the tool. It does this by telling the display system to ignore a specific label that the underlying code library was sending along, since the display system wants to generate those labels itself. Nothing changes for anyone reading the highlighted code, only for the programmers keeping the tool running. This fix is live today.

Now the diagram gets a reliable, consistent name each time it appears, so the page looks the same on first load and on refreshes. If you were watching closely, you might have noticed a tiny flash or shift in the diagram area while the page was still loading; that should no longer happen.

ai.title: Add agent dependency tree visualization to store pages
ai.summary: New API route `/api/agents/[publisherId]/[agentId]/[version]/dependencies` and component `AgentDependencyTree` visualize subagent relationships. Uses batching lookup in `_get.ts` to solve N+1 queries, reducing DB hits to max depth. Integrates into `page.tsx` definition section when `spawnableAgents` exist. Includes Mermaid diagram generation with error boundary fallback.

eli5.text: When you look at a published agent's page on the store, you can now see a visual map of which subagents that agent uses, shown as a clickable, expandable tree. Behind the scenes, the system fetches all of those related agents in as few as six database lookups instead of potentially hundreds, so the page loads quickly. The map only appears on agents that actually have subagents configured, and it lets you expand each branch or jump to any subagent's own page.

ai.title: Add store-lite agents cache for SEO and prefetch
ai.summary: Introduces `getCachedAgentsLite` and `buildAgentsDataLite` to serve a reduced agents dataset. This replaces the full `getCachedAgents` in `healthz`, `sitemap`, and store metadata generation to improve performance. The store client now uses `router.prefetch` on hover/focus/touch to optimize agent detail page navigation.

eli5.text: The assistant directory now loads a smaller version of agent data, so pages like the store, sitemap, and health-check load faster by skipping heavier details. As you browse the store, the site quietly preloads the detail pages of agents you hover over or tap, making those clicks feel instant. This lighter data approach and proactive loading are live today across the store page and related background systems.

ai.summary: agent-tree.ts enforces versioned agent references. parseAgentId now throws on non-publisher/agentId@version formats, removing defaultPublisher fallbacks. ParsedAgentId.version and AgentTreeNode.version change from string | null to string. buildTreeNodeRecursive signature drops defaultPublisher parameter. generateMermaidDiagram always renders version labels.

eli5.text: The system that builds agent trees now requires every agent reference to include a specific version, so references like 'publisher/agentId' or bare 'agentId' will no longer work and will show an error instead. ai.title: SDK getUserInfoFromApiKey requests only needed fields
ai.summary: SDK `getUserInfoFromApiKey` in `sdk/src/impl/database.ts` now requests only missing fields from `/api/v1/me` instead of all `userColumns`. Cache logic updated to merge partial responses, preventing overwrites with incomplete data. This reduces payload size and network overhead for user info retrieval.

eli5.text: The software now asks the server for only the specific pieces of user information it still needs, instead of downloading the entire profile each time, which means faster loads and less data used when checking who you are. If you watched the network traffic, you'd see smaller requests flying back and forth and a local copy of your info that gets filled in piece by piece rather than replaced all at once.
